records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb adding force: true to an unrelated create_table will silently drop and recreate the existing top_topics table (destroying data) on environments that already have it
records.rationale: The diff shows `create_table :top_topics` changed to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` in an unrelated migration. In Rails, force: true drops an existing table before creating it, so re-running migrations (or running in an environment where top_topics already exists) would silently destroy data. The mechanism is verifiable from the diff itself.

records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb referer check breaks embedding for any visitor whose browser suppresses the Referer header (privacy modes, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, HTTPS→HTTP), returning an error page inside the iframe; security relies solely on a client-controlled header
records.rationale: The diff adds `raise Discourse::InvalidAccess.new('invalid referer host') if URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` in EmbedController#ensure_embeddable. If the Referer header is absent (privacy settings, no-referrer policy, cross-protocol), the check fails and returns an error, breaking embedding. The finding's mechanism is verifiable directly from this line.

records.issue_text: TopicEmbed#import interpolates url directly into the HTML of the imported_from footer ("#{url}") without escaping; a URL containing quotes/breakout characters injects arbitrary markup into the post since the regex only checks it starts with http(s)://
records.rationale:
TopicEmbed#import builds the footer via string interpolation: `contents << "
#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")} "` with no escaping, and only guards with `url =~ /^https?\:///`. A URL like `http://x/' onmouseover='...` or containing `>` can break out of the attribute/anchor and inject arbitrary HTML, which is stored as post content (cook_method raw_html) and rendered. The finding's mechanism is directly verifiable in the diff.
